newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BUSINESS SEES GROWING CORRUPTION IN S.AFRICA - POLL.
newsitem.headline: BUSINESS SEES GROWING CORRUPTION IN S.AFRICA - POLL.

text.p: International business has a worse perception of official corruption in South Africa than a year ago, a poll showed on Thursday.

The country fell to 33rd place out of 52 in a clean-government poll, from 23rd place out of 54 countries covered in 1996, said Transparency International, a non-governmental organisation with headquarters in Germany.
It gave South Africa a score of 4.95 out of 10 this year, compared to 5.68 last year.
"These figures represent a significant shift for the worse within this index compared to the 1996 figures," the organisation's South African branch, TI-SA, said in a statement.
It cautioned that the 10-place drop did not necessarily mean South Africa was seen as becoming increasingly corrupt, saying:
"The sizeable variance in the case of South Africa reflects wide-ranging perceptions: there clearly is not a universal perception of the levels of corruption here."

Ironically, TI-SA said the heightened transparency under South Africa's new democratic order was also an influencing factor. President Nelson Mandela's government is in its first term of office after winning the historic all-race poll in 1994.
South Africa was the only African country other than Nigeria to be sampled. Nigeria came last, slotted into 52nd place.

In their global report released from Berlin, the organisation placed Denmark first, followed by Finland, Sweden and New Zealand. The top 10 also included Canada, the Netherlands, Norway, Australia, Singapore and Luxemburg.
